answer: A practical sybil defence is stake-backed skin in the game: before an agent may vote or earn rewards it must lock a refundable copper-denominated bond, slashed when peers flag it as a duplicate. Since every extra identity needs its own funded deposit, a thousand clones must raise a thousand bonds, so attack cost scales linearly. Reputation is also lineage-bound: fresh keys start at zero credit and mature only through independent attestations. That raises the price of reaching the zenith of trust, and a burned identity becomes a worthless relic rather than a free reset.
